title: ISRO Test-Fires Revised PSLV Third Stage After Two Flight Anomalies
excerpt: The strengthened PS3 solid motor was successfully ground-tested at Sriharikota on November 12 after anomalies on PSLV-C61 and PSLV-C62; ISRO says further tests will follow a detailed review of the data, and has not declared the vehicle ready to fly.
body:
• ISRO successfully conducted a ground static test of the PSLV's third stage (PS3) at the Static Test Facility of the Satish Dhawan Space Centre, Sriharikota, on Thursday, November 12, 2026.
  • The revised stage follows anomalies on two missions — PSLV-C61/EOS-09 in May 2025 and PSLV-C62/EOS-N1 in January 2026 — after which ISRO revisited design margins, raw material acceptance criteria, assembly procedures and quality checks, and improved the nozzle design.
  • ISRO has not declared the vehicle ready to fly again: it said further tests are planned after a detailed analysis and review of this test's data.
  • No root cause for the two anomalies, and no date or mission for the revised stage's first flight, has been announced.

The Indian Space Research Organisation has fired the revised third stage of its Polar Satellite Launch Vehicle on the ground — the clearest step yet toward returning the PSLV to flight after two missions were lost to third-stage anomalies. ISRO said the ground static test of the PS3 stage was conducted successfully on Thursday at the Static Test Facility of the Satish Dhawan Space Centre in Sriharikota, according to the agency's statement reported by ANI via Devdiscourse.

What was changed

The test follows a comprehensive review of the stage's configuration after anomalies during the PSLV-C61/EOS-09 mission — launched on May 18, 2025 — and the PSLV-C62/EOS-N1 mission on January 12, 2026, which carried EOS-N1 and 15 additional payloads from Indian and international startups and academic institutions. ISRO said the PS3 configuration was revisited with particular attention to design margins, raw material acceptance criteria, assembly procedures and quality checks, and that the configuration was strengthened, with essential improvements made to the nozzle design to enhance design margins. The new version of the PS3 solid motor was then built and tested on November 12.

What a static test does — and does not — prove

A static firing shows whether the motor and its supporting systems perform under controlled conditions on the ground. It cannot reproduce every condition of an orbital launch, and ISRO's statement does not claim the full vehicle is cleared for flight. The agency has not disclosed a single root cause for the two anomalies, and nothing in its statement establishes that both flights failed for the same reason, World of Now noted in its account of the announcement.

What's next

The next milestone is analysis, not a launch date. ISRO said that based on a detailed analysis and review of the test data, further tests are planned; it has not announced how many, when they will run, or which mission will first fly the revised stage. The PS3 is the solid third stage of the four-stage PSLV, one of India's principal routes to orbit for Earth-observation, scientific and commercial satellites.
